sample_data.reset_instructions: Use Reset Demo State in the application to clear reviewer decisions for the active case.

problem_solving_method: ReconFlow uses a deterministic multi-pass reconciliation method. It first validates and profiles the POS and settlement datasets, normalizes different transaction reference formats, discovers high-trust seed pairs, and learns the dominant settlement fee and clock offset from the data. It then scores possible transaction pairs using semantic reference, fee-adjusted amount and corrected-time evidence. Strong and unique matches are automatically reconciled, while ambiguous or conflicting cases are sent to human review with clear explanations. Reviewers can Accept, Reject or manually pair records, and every decision immediately recalculates the reconciliation result and financial totals.

major_design_decisions: Used deterministic multi-signal reconciliation instead of an LLM for financial matching so results remain reproducible, testable and explainable.
Separated candidate evidence from auto-match safety so a high similarity score alone cannot automatically clear an ambiguous financial record.
Used semantic reference normalization together with learned settlement-fee and clock-offset relationships instead of exact string, amount and timestamp matching.
Used high-trust seed pairs to infer the relationship between the POS and settlement systems instead of hardcoding case-specific fee or time-offset values.
Used a Next.js modular monolith with a same-origin API to reduce deployment complexity and failure points during the hackathon.
Stored reviewer decisions and active-case state per case in browser localStorage for the MVP instead of introducing database infrastructure.
Represented money internally using integer poisha to reduce floating-point precision problems in financial calculations.
Preferred conservative human review over unsafe automatic matching when duplicates or competing candidates create ambiguity.
known_limitations: The MVP loads the organizer-provided JSON fixture instead of supporting arbitrary CSV or XLSX uploads.
Reviewer state is stored in browser localStorage and is not synchronized across users or devices.
There is no authentication, shared audit database or multi-user approval workflow.
The MVP does not directly integrate with merchant POS systems, banks or settlement providers.
The learned fee and clock relationships are deterministic case-level inferences rather than continuously trained machine-learning models.
